mappings.note: Gametes fusing to give a zygote is the first step of the reproduction process LO-65 names. Not LO-62, because no mode of reproduction is classified.
The developing zygote becoming an embryo is a stage of the reproductive process. Not LO-69, because no organ is named or drawn.
The foetus as the stage where body parts are recognisable is a stage of development. Grouped with the other process items.
Animals that give birth being viviparous is the viviparous/oviparous differentiation named verbatim in LO-61. Not LO-62, whose example is the sexual/asexual split.
Egg-laying animals being oviparous is the other half of the same differentiation. Coded with its counterpart.
A fertilised ovum developing into a baby in the uterus describes where development happens, part of the process. Not LO-69, which is used for items naming reproductive organs as such.
Picking the hermaphrodite animal classifies organisms by their reproductive arrangement. Not LO-61, because a class is assigned rather than two groups contrasted.
Which organism needs two parents is the sexual/asexual classification LO-62 names verbatim. Not LO-65, because no process is explained.
What is involved in sexual reproduction is the same sexual/asexual classification. Grouped with the two-parent item.
An organism with both sex organs being hermaphrodite classifies by reproductive arrangement. Duplicate in substance of the hermaphrodite item.
Fertilisation as the fusion of gametes is the process explanation. Not LO-62, because no mode is classified.
Amoeba reproducing by binary fission assigns an organism to an asexual mode. Not LO-65, because the mode rather than the mechanism is asked.
Hydra reproducing by budding assigns an organism to an asexual mode. Grouped with the Amoeba item.
Which animals fertilise externally differentiates animals by their mode of fertilisation. Not LO-65, which covers what fertilisation is rather than which animals do it one way.
Where a test-tube baby actually develops applies reproductive science to a real medical technique. Not LO-65, because the item turns on the technology rather than the biology.
Which animal's young resemble their parents differentiates animals by their development. Not LO-65, which is used for metamorphosis as a process.
Which animal's young differ from their parents is the mirror differentiation. Coded with its counterpart.
Animals with separate sexes being unisexual classifies by reproductive arrangement. Kept apart from the hermaphrodite items as its opposite case.
What a bird's egg is called belongs to the vocabulary of the reproductive process. Not LO-61, because the item does not sort birds against other animals.
Naming the male reproductive organ is the human reproductive anatomy LO-69 names verbatim. Not LO-65, which covers the process rather than the parts.
Naming the female reproductive organ is the same anatomy outcome. Coded with its counterpart.
Fertilisation as the fusion of egg and sperm is a process explanation. Duplicate in substance of the gamete-fusion item.
Which animals fertilise internally differentiates animals by mode of fertilisation. Coded with the external-fertilisation item.
Identifying the male reproductive organs is reproductive anatomy. Grouped with the other organ items.
Which animals lay eggs is the oviparous side of LO-61's verbatim differentiation. Coded with the other oviparous items.
Internal fertilisation happening inside the female body explains the process. Not LO-61, because no animals are being sorted here.
A tadpole becoming a frog by metamorphosis explains a developmental process. Not LO-61, which is used where animals are sorted by whether young resemble parents.
The single nucleus of a zygote is a detail of the fertilisation process. Not LO-68, because no slide is prepared or described.
How many modes of reproduction animals have is the sexual/asexual classification. Not LO-65, because no process is explained.
Binary fission observed in Amoeba assigns an organism to an asexual mode. Duplicate in substance of the Amoeba item.
Where asexual reproduction is seen is the sexual/asexual classification. Grouped with the other mode items.
Budding as Hydra's mode assigns an organism to an asexual mode. Duplicate in substance of the Hydra item.
Animals that bear live young being viviparous is LO-61's verbatim differentiation. Coded with the other viviparous items.
What a sperm is made of is reproductive structure, which LO-69 covers with the reproductive organs. Not LO-68, because no slide is prepared.
Ova being formed in the ovary names a reproductive organ and its function. Grouped with the other organ items.
Internal fertilisation taking place inside the body explains the process. Duplicate in substance of the earlier internal-fertilisation item.
Development of the fertilised egg in the uterus describes the human reproductive process. Not LO-69, because the process rather than the organ list is the point.
The zygote as the cell formed at fertilisation is a process term. Duplicate in substance of the gamete-fusion items.
Where sperm and ovum fuse describes the fertilisation process. Not LO-69, because the event rather than the anatomy is asked.

Finding the incorrect set of reproductive terms tests the vocabulary of reproduction in animals as a whole, which is what LO-65 covers. No narrower outcome fits, since the sets span organs, gametes and stages rather than one of them.
